changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For prospects whose online checkouts are failing, especially on high-value orders, swap the average-uplift claim for a figure built on their own numbers: Stop losing your biggest orders at the last step. Your [one-in-N] failed checkouts, concentrated in your biggest baskets, are worth $[X] a year. Fill N from the prospect's own failure rate and X from their own data. Keep the Authorization Boost / Adaptive Acceptance names as the how, not the headline.
changes.why: We showed 'the average improvement in acceptance' and the CFO concluded 'the same thing', while the customer described the problem as 'orders dying at the last step' on 'the big baskets' using her own dashboard number, which we never turned into dollars.

changes.change: Add a standard proof offer for deals where the finance approver won't meet us: Send us a three-month decline export and we'll give you a one-page business case showing what your failed orders are worth next to the rate difference. Position it as the page the champion hands to the CFO and controller, not an optional extra, and offer it before pricing.
changes.why: The champion asked for 'a one-page business case' to hand the CFO and got the deck and pricing, so the controller's side-by-side carried only 'Our quote' against the bank's rate, while Farah's decline analysis was on offer and could have filled that gap.

changes.change: For prospects processing through their bank who can't get answers on failures, add a line on explanation, not just acceptance: Your processor can't tell you why the card says no. We'll show you why your big orders fail and what we'd do about it. Use it early, before the incumbent's rate counter turns the conversation into a rate comparison.
changes.why: The customer's second pain was that she 'couldn't get a straight answer from the processor on why', and our explanation of 'Why big orders fail, what we'd do about it' had her 'nodding the whole way', but once the bank 'sharpened the rate' 'every email was the rate'.
